recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR source change is recommended; future corrections to medication-manufacturingBatch should be made in HL7/fhir-extensions rather than reintroducing the extension definition into core.
issue_request: FHIR-29569 was a Published Pharmacy change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5, asking to add Expiration Date Classification to Medication.Batch. The Jira description used date-type wording, but the final summary and the implemented issue family identify this as a classification/rationale attribute, with a resolution to create a core extension.
initial_application: No implementation commit was found whose message explicitly names FHIR-29569. Git history shows commit 52f3ef3d50 added manufacturingBatch.expirationDateClassification to the old core Medication extension spreadsheet as a CodeableConcept, commit 33b409a4b6 generated structuredefinition-extension-medication-manufacturingBatch.xml with that slice, and commit dd468d4f17 later removed the core extension source when R5 extensions moved out of HL7/fhir.
additional_context: Medication is still active in core, but historical Medication.batch paths map to Medication.instance and core retains only the medication-manufacturingBatch OID registry entry. The Extension Pack source applies medication-manufacturingBatch to Medication.batch and defines expirationDateClassification as a CodeableConcept slice. Pharmacy minutes for 2020-11-09 record the PQ/CMC block vote including FHIR-29569 to add a core extension; a 2022 Zulip thread shows implementer use of the same extension family and no conflicting later decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit. No HL7/fhir source was changed because the current source of truth for the extension is HL7/fhir-extensions and it already carries the requested slice.
